title: CERTIFIED TAX ACCOUNTANT ACT
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Act is to promote the smooth execution of tax administration and the appropriate performance of the duty to pay taxes by establishing the certified tax accountant system.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 1-2 (Mission of Certified Tax Accountants) Any certified tax accountant, as a tax specialist of public character, shall be charged with the mission to protect the rights and interests of taxpayers and to contribute to having them conscientiously perform their duty to pay taxes.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 2 (Duties of Certified Tax Accountants) Any certified tax accountant shall engage in the following activities or services (hereinafter referred to as "tax agent services") with the authority delegated by taxpayers, etc.: <Amended on May 2, 2011; Jan. 19, 2016; Dec. 26, 2017>
  1. Reporting, filing applications or requests (including requests for pre-assessment review, objections, requests for examination and request for trial) with regard to taxes by proxy (including requests for administrative trial by proxy on development charges under the Restitution of Development Gains Act);
  2. Preparing statements of tax adjustment and other tax-related documents;
  3. Preparing books by proxy for filing returns on taxes;
  4. Providing consultations or advices on taxes;
  5. Stating a taxpayer's opinion by proxy related to investigations, dispositions, etc. by a tax office;
  6. Filing objections by proxy to public notice of the officially assessed individual land prices, the prices of detached houses and the prices of multi-family houses under the Act on the Public Announcement of Real Estate Values;
  7. Verifying any tax-related return document prepared by the relevant certified tax accountant: Provided, That if a taxpayer has prepared a return document personally, or if it is impossible to verify a return document because a certified tax accountant who prepared the return document has suspended or discontinued his or her business, a certified tax accountant who makes tax adjustment, prepares books by proxy, or provides consulting services may verify the return document for such taxpayer;
  8. Verifying whether a tax payer files a return conscientiously pursuant to the Income Tax Act or the Corporate Tax Act;
  9. Other services incidental to the activities or services referred to in subparagraphs 1 through 8.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 2-2 (Prohibition of Introduction or Arrangement for Introduction of Tax Agent Services) No person shall introduce or arrange for the introduction of tax agent services prescribed in Article 2 to certified tax accounts, clerks thereof, tax accounting corporations or employees thereof and receive or demand the consideration therefor.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021]

Article 3 (Qualifications for Certified Tax Accountants) Any of the following persons shall be qualified as a certified tax accountant: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A person who has passed a qualification examination for certified tax accountants referred to in Article 5;
  2. Deleted; <Jan. 26, 2012>
  3. Deleted. <Dec. 26, 2017>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 3-2 (Certified Tax Accountant Qualification Screening Committee) (1) A Certified Tax Accountant Qualification Screening Committee may be established within the National Tax Service to deliberate on the following matters with respect to the acquisition of qualifications for certified tax accountants:
  1. Matters concerning examinations, such as the subjects of a qualification examination for certified tax accountants;
  2. Decision on the number of persons to be selected through examination;
  3. Requirements for persons eligible for partial exemption from examination;
  4. Other important matters concerning the acquisition of qualifications for certified tax accountants.
  (2) Matters necessary for the organization, operation, etc. of the Certified Tax Accountant Qualification Screening Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 4 (Grounds for Disqualification of Certified Tax Accountants) None of the following persons shall be entitled to file for registration under Article 6: <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A minor;
  2. A person under adult guardianship or a person under limited guardianship;
  3. A person who was declared bankrupt and has not been reinstated;
  4. A person in whose case three years have not passed since he or she was dismissed or released from office in consequence of impeachment or disciplinary action;
  5. A person in whose case three years have not passed since he or she was expelled or his or her registration was revoked in consequence of disciplinary action taken under this Act, the Certified Public Accountant Act or the Attorney-at-Law Act, and a person who has been suspended and the suspension period is not over;
  6. A person who is in the period for rejection of registration under Article 17 (3);
  7. A person in whose case three years have not passed since his or her imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment declared by a court was completely executed (including where the execution is deemed to have been completed) or exempted;
  8. A person in whose case one year has not passed since the suspension of the execution of his or her imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment declared by a court was completed;
  9. A person under suspension of the sentence of his or her imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment declared by a court;
  10. A person in whose case three years have not passed since the punishment by a fine imposed on him or her under this Act and the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act was completely executed or determined not to be executed, or a person in whose case three years have not passed since the disposition of notification to him or her under the Procedure for the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act was conducted as notified.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

CHAPTER II EXAMINATIONS

Article 5 (Qualification Examinations for Certified Tax Accountants) (1) A qualification examination for certified tax accountants shall be comprised of a preliminary test and a secondary test implemented by the Minister of Economy and Finance.
  (2) No person falling under any of subparagraphs 2 through 10 of Article 4 as at the date applicants who finally pass a qualification examination for certified tax accountants are announced may apply for the examination. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2018>
  (3) The subjects of a qualification examination for certified tax accountants referred to in paragraph (1) and other matters necessary for such examination shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 5-2 (Partial Exemption from Examinations) (1) Any of the following persons shall be exempted from a preliminary test: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Nov. 23, 2021>
  1. A person who has been engaged in the administrative affairs with respect to national taxes (excluding customs; hereinafter the same shall apply) for at least 10 years;
  2. A public official of Grade V or higher who has been engaged in the administrative affairs with respect to local taxes for at least 10 years or a member in general service of the Senior Executive Service who has been engaged in such service for at least five years;
  3. A person who has been engaged in the administrative affairs with respect to local taxes for at least 20 years;
  4. A person of the rank of captain or above who has served for at least 10 years in the military as an officer in charge of financial affairs.
  (2) Any of the following persons shall be exempted from all subjects of a preliminary test and some of the subjects of a secondary test prescribed by Presidential Decree to the extent not exceeding 1/2 of the number of subjects of a secondary test: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A public official of Grade V or higher who has been engaged in the administrative affairs with respect to national taxes for at least 10 years or a member in general service of the Senior Executive Service who has been engaged in such service for at least five years;
  2. A person who has been engaged in the administrative affairs with respect to national taxes for at least 20 years.
  (3) Paragraphs (1) and (2) shall not apply to any of the following persons: <Amended on Dec. 26, 2017; Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A person dismissed or released from office by impeachment or disciplinary action;
  2. A person in whose case two years have not elapsed since he or she was subject to a disposition such as demotion or suspension of business operation.
  (4) Any person who has passed a preliminary test shall only be exempted from a preliminary test to be implemented next time. <Amended Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 5-3 (Sanctions for Wrongdoers) The Minister of Economy and Finance shall take a disposition to suspend or nullify an examination that any of the following persons has taken, and place restrictions on his or her eligibility to take an examination for five years from the date on which such disposition has been taken:
  1. Any person applying for an examination by improper means;
  2. Any person engaging in cheating behaviors during an examination.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jul. 25, 2011]

CHAPTER III REGISTRATION

Article 6 (Registration) (1) Where a person qualified as a certified tax accountant after having passed a qualification examination for certified tax accountants referred to in Article 5 intends to commence the tax agent services, he or she shall register matters prescribed by Presidential Decree including his or her name, the name and location of the relevant office, whether he or she has resigned from the position of tax official under subparagraph 17 of Article 2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes (hereinafter referred to as “certified tax accountant who resigned as public official”), and number of certificate of qualification, etc. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (2) Registration referred to in paragraph (1) may be renewed as prescribed by Presidential Decree. In such cases, the period of renewal shall be at least three years.
  (3) Where a person applying for registration pursuant to paragraph (1) falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance shall reject such registration: <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016>
  1. Where he or she becomes disqualified as referred to in Article 4;
  2. Where he or she fails to receive in-service education referred to in Article 12-6 (1);
  3. Where he or she serves concurrently as a public official or engages in profit-making business, in violation of Article 16.
  (4) Where the Minister of Economy and Finance rejects registration pursuant to paragraph (3), he or she shall notify the applicant of the ground for such rejection within 30 days after receipt of the application for registration.
  (5) Where there is a change to any registered matter with regard to a certified tax accountant registered pursuant to paragraph (1), such as the commencement, suspension, or closure of business or the establishment, relocation, or closure of an office, he or she shall report to the Minister of Economy and Finance thereon, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly Inserted on Jan. 1, 2013; Nov. 23, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]
  [Paragraph (1) of this Article was amended following the decision of nonconformity to the Constitution by the Constitutional Court on Novemver 23, 2021 in accordance with Act No. 18521 (Apr. 26, 2018)]

Article 7 (Revocation of Registration) Where a certified tax accountant falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance shall revoke his or her registration: <Amended on Dec. 29, 2015>
  1. Where he or she is subject to a disposition of disciplinary action pursuant to Article 17 (1) and (2) 1;
  2. Where he or she becomes disqualified as referred to in Article 4;
  3. Where the relevant certified tax accountant requests the revocation of his or her registration;
  4. Where the relevant certified tax accountant discontinues his or her business;
  5. Where his or her registration is revoked under the Certified Public Accountant Act or the Attorney-at-Law Act;
  6. Where he or she is deceased.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 8 (Notification of Registration or Revocation of Registration) Where the Minister of Economy and Finance files for registration pursuant to Article 6 or revokes the registration pursuant to Article 7, he or she shall notify the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants, the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants, or the Korean Bar Association with which the person qualified as a certified tax accountant is affiliated as a member (hereinafter referred to as the "Association he or she is affiliated with") of such registration or revocation. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013; Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

CHAPTER IV RIGHTS AND DUTIES

Article 9 (Affixing Names and Seals) When any person who has filed for registration under Article 6 submits a return, an application, a written request, or other documents relating to taxes he or she has prepared to the relevant agency on behalf of a taxpayer, etc., he or she shall affix his or her name and seal to such document. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 10 (Investigation Notices) If a tax official deems it necessary to conduct an investigation with respect to a return, an application or a written request submitted under Article 9, he or she shall notify the relevant certified tax accountant of the time and place of such investigation.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 11 (Confidentiality) No current or former certified tax accountant or his or her current or former clerk shall divulge any confidential information he or she has learned in the course of performing his or her duties, except as otherwise provided in other statutes or regulations. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 12 (Duty to Maintain Conscientiousness) (1) Every certified tax accountant shall perform his or her duties with conscientiousness and maintain his or her dignity.
  (2) No certified tax accountant shall conceal the truth intentionally or make false statements.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 12-2 (Prohibition of Consultation on Tax Evasion) No certified tax accountant or his or her clerk shall be involved in or aid affairs that a taxpayer evades a tax, obtains a tax refund or deduction by fraud or other improper means or consult the same, or do any act similar thereto.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 12-3 (Prohibition of Title Lending) (1) No certified tax accountant shall allow another person to provide tax agent services by using his or her name or trade name, or lend his or her certificate of qualification or registration to another person. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (2) No one shall borrow a name or trade name from a certified tax accountant to provide tax agent services or borrow his or her certificate of qualification or registration. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (3) No one shall arrange for the acts prohibited under paragraphs (1) and (2). <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 12-4 (Prohibition of Provision of Money and Goods) No certified tax accountant shall act as follows:
  1. Providing, or promising to offer goods or entertainments to a public official;
  2. Assisting an act referred to in subparagraph (1).
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 2, 2016]
  [Previous Article 12-4 moved to Article 12-5 <Mar. 2, 2016>]

Article 12-5 (Clerk) (1) A certified tax accountant may employ clerks to assist him or her in appropriately conducting his or her services.
  (2) A certified tax accountant shall be responsible for guiding and supervising clerks referred to in paragraph (1) to appropriately conduct his or her services.
  (3) Necessary matters concerning the qualification, number, training, etc. of clerks may be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]
  [Moved from Article 12-4; previous Article 12-5 moved to Article 12-6 <Mar. 2, 2016>]

Article 12-6 (Education for Certified Tax Accountants) (1) Where a person qualified as a certified tax accountant intends to commence tax agent services, he or she shall receive in-house education for at least six months before filing for registration referred to in Article 6, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy and Finance: Provided, That where a person partially exempted from examinations pursuant to Article 5-2 (1) or (2) passes a qualification examination for certified tax accountants, he or she shall receive in-house education for at least one month. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013; Jun. 9, 2020>
  (2) A certified tax accountant making a registration pursuant to Article 6 (1) shall receive the refresher training for not less than eight hours every year to reinforce expertise and ethics: Provided, That, this shall not apply to cases falling under any of the causes prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as where it is inappropriate for a certified tax account to receive the refresher training, due to his or her illness, temporary closure of business, or otherwise. <Newly Inserted on Jan. 1, 2013>
  (3) Necessary matters concerning the subjects, place, timing, and completion methods of the education referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy and Finance. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]
  [Moved from Article 12-5 <Mar. 2, 2016>]

Article 13 (Establishment of Offices) (1) A certified tax accountant may establish only one office to provide tax agent services.
  (2) No certified tax accountant shall establish a separate office only for tax agent services where he or she simultaneously engages in the business of a qualified person prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as a certified public accountant, attorney-at-law, certified judicial scrivener, patent attorney, customs broker, certified public appraiser, certified public labor attorney, licensed real estate agent, certified management consultant, certified technical consultant, certified administrative scrivener or any other person with qualifications similar thereto.
  (3) Deleted. <Dec. 29, 2015>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 13-2 Deleted. <Dec. 30, 2002>

Article 14 (Reporting on Business Performance) (1) A certified tax accountant (including those belonging to a corporation or organization) shall prepare and retain a statement of business performance of the previous year, and submit it, by the end of July 31 every year, to the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants (or the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants in the case of a certified public accountant eligible to register as a certified tax accountant under Article 2 (1) of the Addenda to the Certified Tax Accountant Act (No. 7032)). In such cases, a statement of business performance shall be prepared separately, based on features of services such as reporting or filing applications by proxy, request by proxy, or tax investigation by proxy, advice or consulting, or tax adjustment, and shall include details prescribed by Presidential Decree such as contract prices and the number of contracts for services, or whether or not he or she is a certified tax accountant who resigned as public official. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020; Nov. 23, 2021>
  (2) Matters necessary for preparing and reporting of, or methods and period of storage of a statement of business performance under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 31, 2018]

Article 14-2 (Prohibition on Advertising Connections) No certified tax accountant or his or her clerk shall advertise that he or she may have influence by making reference to personal relations with tax official to win a contract for tax agent services.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 31, 2018]

Article 14-3 (Restriction on Being Awarded Contracts) (1) No certified tax accountant who retires after having served as a public official of Grade V or higher (including a public official in political service and a member of the Senior Executive Service; where a person goes into honorable retirement pursuant to Article 74-2 of the State Public Officials Act after receiving special promotion pursuant to Article 40-4 (1) 4 of that Act, referring to a person of at least Grade V before special promotion) or a grade equivalent thereto and commences business as a certified tax account (hereinafter referred to as "certified tax accountant who resigned as public official and is subject to restriction on being awarded contracts") shall be awarded a contract for tax agent services with respect to affairs handled by State agencies, such as the Ministry of Economy and Finance, the National Tax Service, and the Tax Tribunal, where he worked one year prior to his or her retirement until the date of retirement, for one year from the date of his or her retirement: Provided, That this shall not apply where a contract is awarded to a public representative prescribed in Article 59-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes for the purposes of public interest, such as tax agent services, and a relative prescribed in Article 767 of the Civil Act is a party to a contract for tax agent services.
  (2) Cases in which contracts shall not be awarded under paragraph (1) shall include the following:
  1. Where a certified tax accountant who resigned as public official and is subject to restriction on being awarded contracts is designated as a certified tax accountant in charge of a tax accounting corporation, etc.;
  2. Where a certified tax accountant who resigned as public official and is subject to restriction on being awarded contracts is essentially awarded a contract acting as a de facto tax agent by borrowing the name from another certified tax accountant or tax accounting corporation, etc.;
  3. In cases of a tax accounting corporation, etc., where a certified tax accountant who resigned as public official and is subject to restriction on being awarded contracts is not indicated as a certified tax accountant, but receives a fee by participating in providing tax agent services.
  (3) The scope of State agencies referred to paragraph (1), the scope of affairs performed by State agencies, the scope of contracts for public Interest, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021]

Article 15 (Ban on Acquisition by Transfer of Rights in Dispute) No certified tax accountant shall acquire any right in a dispute by transfer.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16 (Prohibition of Holding Concurrent Office as Public Official or Engaging in Business for Profit) (1) No certified tax accountant shall serve concurrently as a public official: Provided, That this shall not apply where he or she falls under any of the following cases:
  1. Where he or she becomes a member of the National Assembly or a member of any local council;
  2. Where he or she becomes a public official who need not work on a full-time basis;
  3. Where he or she conducts affairs entrusted by the State, a local government and other public institution (hereinafter referred to as "public institution").
  (2) No certified tax accountant shall, with the exception of the following, become an employee of any person running business for profit, or an executive officer, executive or employee of a profit-making corporation:
  1. Giving lectures in the educational fields, such as a school and a private educational institute (excluding a full-time lecturer);
  2. Working as a non-standing executive of a profit-making corporation.
  (3) Paragraphs (1) and (2) shall not apply to any certified tax accountant whose business is temporarily closed.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-2 (Guarantee of Liability for Damage) Where a certified tax accountant (excluding a certified tax accountant affiliated with a tax accounting corporation) inflicts damage by intention or negligence on any mandator while performing his or her duties, he or she shall take necessary measures to guarantee the liability for such damage, such as purchasing an insurance policy, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

CHAPTER IV-2 TAX ACCOUNTING CORPORATION

Article 16-3 (Establishment) (1) A certified tax accountant may establish a tax accounting corporation to provide their services in a systematic and professional manner.
  (2) The following matters shall be entered in the articles of incorporation of a tax accounting corporation: <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. Objectives;
  2. Name;
  3. Location of its principal office and branch offices;
  4. Names, resident registration numbers (alien registration numbers in case of employees who are foreign-certified tax consultants) and addresses of employees and directors;
  5. The amount of one share in equity investment;
  6. The number of shares held by each employee;
  7. The gross amount of capital;
  8. Matters concerning the coverage of deficits;
  9. Matters concerning general meetings of employees;
  10. Matters concerning the representative director;
  11. Matters concerning its services;
  12. If the period of existence and the reasons for dissolution are prescribed, such period and reasons.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-4 (Registration of Tax Accounting Corporations) (1) When a tax accounting corporation intends to provide its services, it shall file for the registration with the Minister of Economy and Finance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) Any tax accounting corporation that intends to file for the registration pursuant to paragraph (1) shall meet the following requirements:
  1. It shall employ employees, directors, etc., pursuant to Article 16-5;
  2. Its capital shall be at least 200 million won, pursuant to Article 16-6 (1);
  3. The details of application documents for registration shall comply with this Act or an order issued under this Act;
  4. No false entry shall be made in application documents for registration.
  (3) Where any person filing for registration fails to meet the requirements referred to in paragraph (2), the Minister of Economy and Finance may reject registration, and where application documents for registration are found to be incomplete, the Minister of Economy and Finance may request the applicant to supplement such documents within a prescribed period.
  (4) Matters necessary for procedures for registration of tax accounting corporations, required documents, etc., pursuant to paragraph (1), shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-5 (Employees and Directors) (1) The employees of tax accounting corporations shall be certified tax accountants (including foreign-certified tax consultants employed at the relevant tax accounting corporation) and their number shall be at least three. <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016>
  (2) A tax accounting corporation shall have at least three directors. In such cases, none of the following persons shall become a director: <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A person not employed by the corporation;
  2. A person who has been ordered to be suspended under Article 17 and the suspension period is not over;
  3. A person who once served as a director (limited to a person who served as a director when a reason for the revocation of registration or the suspension of business arose) of a tax accounting corporation, the registration of which has been revoked or business of which has been suspended pursuant to Article 16-5 (1), and in whose case three years have not passed after the revocation of registration or whose business has been suspended;
  4. A foreign-certified tax consultant referred to in subparagraph 1 of Article 19-2.
  (3) A tax accounting corporation shall have at least five certified tax accountants among directors and employees.
  (4) Any certified tax accountant who is not a director among certified tax accountants under paragraph (3) (hereinafter referred to as "affiliated certified tax accountant") shall be a person whose business is no longer under suspension after having been ordered to be suspended pursuant to Article 17. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (5) A tax accounting corporation shall have a representative director, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (6) If an employee of a tax accounting corporation falls under any of the following cases, he or she shall duly leave from the tax accounting corporation:
  1. Where his or her registration is revoked pursuant to Article 7;
  2. Where any reason prescribed by the articles of incorporation arises;
  3. Where a general meeting of employees passes a resolution.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-6 (Capital Stock) (1) The capital stock of each tax accounting corporation shall be at least 200 million won.
  (2) If the amount remaining after subtracting the total amount of liabilities from the gross amount of assets on the statement of financial position at the end of the preceding business year falls short of the capital stock referred to in paragraph (1), the relevant tax accounting corporation shall supplement the shortage with donations made by employees or increase its capital stock within six months after the end of each business year. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (3) In cases of donations made by employees under paragraph (2), such donations shall be included in special profits.
  (4) Where a tax accounting corporation fails to supplement a shortage or increase its capital as prescribed in paragraph (2), the Minister of Economy and Finance may order the relevant tax accounting corporation to supplement such shortage or increase its capital within a prescribed period.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-7 (Compensation Reserve) (1) Each tax accounting corporation shall either accumulate the compensation reserve or purchase damage liability insurance in each business year, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, in order to guarantee the liability for damage it may inflict on any mandator while providing its services.
  (2) None of the compensation reserve or damage liability insurance referred to in paragraph (1) shall be used for the purposes other than the compensation for damage, and a contract for damage liability insurance shall not be cancelled or terminated without approval from the Minister of Economy and Finance.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-8 (Restrictions on Making Equity Investments in other Corporations) (1) Every tax accounting corporation shall be prohibited from making equity investments in other corporations or from providing debt guarantees for a third person in excess of the amount calculated by multiplying the rate prescribed by Presidential Decree by its equity capital.
  (2) The equity capital referred to in paragraph (1) means the amount calculated by subtracting the total amount of liabilities (excluding the compensation reserve) from the gross amount of assets on the statement of financial position at the end of the preceding business year. <Amended on Nov. 23, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-9 (Name) (1) Every tax accounting corporation shall use a name that includes a tax accounting corporation.
  (2) No entity, other than a tax accounting corporation registered pursuant to Article 16-4 (1), shall use the name tax accounting corporation or any other name similar thereto.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-10 (Offices) (1) Every tax accounting corporation may establish branch offices, along with its principal office, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) No directors and certified tax accountants affiliated with a tax accounting corporation shall have a separate office other than a tax accounting corporation they are affiliated with.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-11 (Methods of Providing Services) (1) A tax accounting corporation shall provide services in the name of the corporation and, when it provides services, it shall designate a certified tax accountant in charge of such services: Provided, That where it designates an affiliated certified tax accountant, it shall designate a director jointly with the affiliated certified tax accountant.
  (2) When a director or an affiliated certified tax accountant designated pursuant to paragraph (1) provides services designated, he or she shall represent the tax accounting corporation he or she is affiliated with, respectively.
  (3) Documents prepared by a tax accounting corporation in connection with its services shall be marked with the name of the corporation and a certified tax accountant in charge of such services shall affix his or her name and seal thereon.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-12 (Prohibition from Providing Competitive Services) (1) No director or certified tax accountant affiliated with a tax accounting corporation shall provide services belonging to the scope of services provided by the tax accounting corporation for the sake of himself, herself or any third person, or become a director or certified tax accountant affiliated with another tax accounting corporation.
  (2) No former director or certified tax accountant affiliated with a tax accounting corporation shall, after his or her resignation, provide services as a certified tax accountant with regard to the services that the tax accounting corporation has provided or approved during the period he or she was affiliated therewith: Provided, That this shall not apply where the tax accounting corporation agrees to the provision of such services by him or her. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-13 (Dissolution) (1) A tax accounting corporation shall be dissolved for any of the following reasons:
  1. Any reason prescribed by the articles of incorporation;
  2. A resolution at a general meeting of employees;
  3. A merger;
  4. Revocation of registration;
  5. Bankruptcy;
  6. Orders or adjudications issued by the court.
  (2) Where any reason for dissolution provided for in the provisions of paragraph (1) (excluding the revocation of registration referred to in subparagraph 4) arises, a tax accounting corporation shall notify the Minister of Economy and Finance of the fact.
  (3) Where a tax accounting corporation is dissolved for any reason specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) (excluding a merger referred to in subparagraph 3), it shall separately deposit an amount equivalent to the amount of the compensation reserve (referring to the amount on the statement of financial position at the end of the business year immediately prior to the dissolution) accumulated in accordance with Article 16-7 (1) with the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants established pursuant to Article 18. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013; Nov. 23, 2021>
  (4) Matters necessary for the management and operation of the money deposited under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-14 (Reporting on Amendments of Articles of Incorporation) When a tax accounting corporation amends any of the following matters among the matters entered in the articles of incorporation pursuant to Article 16-3 (2), it shall report thereon to the Minister of Economy and Finance without delay: <Amended on Mar. 2, 2016>
  1. Objectives;
  2. Name;
  3. Location of its principal office and branch offices;
  4. Names and resident registration numbers (alien registration numbers in case of employees who are foreign-certified tax consultants) of employees and directors;
  5. The gross amount of capital (limited to decrease of capital);
  6. Matters concerning the representative director;
  7. Matters concerning the services.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-15 (Revocation of Registration) (1) Where a tax accounting corporation falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance may revoke its registration, or issue an order to wholly or partially suspend tax agent services for up to one year: Provided, That where it falls under subparagraphs 1 through 3, he or she shall revoke its registration: <Amended on Dec. 29, 2015; Mar. 2, 2016>
  1. Where it files for the registration pursuant to Article 16-4 (1) by fraud or other improper means;
  2. Where it which fails to meet the requirements prescribed in Article 16-5 (1) through (3) or 16-6 (1) fails to supplement the same within six months;
  3. Where it conducts business, in violation of an order to suspend his or her business;
  4. Where it fails to comply with an order of the Minister of Economy and Finance to supplement a shortage or increase its capital pursuant to Article 16-6 (4);
  5. Where it violates Articles 16-5 (4) and (5), 16-7, 16-8, 16-9 (1), 16-11 or 16-14, or Articles 11, 12, 12-2 through 12-5, 15 and 19-14 applied mutatis mutandis pursuant to Article 16-16 (1).
  (2) The Minister of Economy and Finance shall hold a hearing if he or she intends to revoke registration of any tax accounting corporation in accordance with paragraph (1).
  (3) When the Minister of Economy and Finance revokes the registration of a tax accounting corporation or issue an order to suspend tax agent services pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall notify the relevant tax accounting corporation, the Korea Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants, and the Commissioner of the National Tax Service of the specific grounds therefor without delay, and publish an announcement of the details thereof in the Official Gazette or on the website of the Ministry of Economy and Finance. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (4) The Korea Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall disclose the matters notified pursuant to paragraph (3) by posting them on its website for at least three months. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (5) Matters necessary for the notification and public announcement under paragraph (3) and the disclosure under paragraph (4) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 16-16 (Application Mutatis Mutandis to Tax Accounting Corporations) (1) Articles 10 through 12, 12-2 through 12-5, 14-2, 15 and 17 (4) (excluding where a tax accounting corporation falls under Article 16-15 (1) 1) shall apply mutatis mutandis to tax accounting corporations. In such cases, "certified tax accountant" shall be construed as "tax accounting corporation", and "disciplinary action" in Article 17 (4) shall be construed as "revocation of registration and suspension of business." <Amended on Dec. 29, 2015; Mar. 2, 2016; Dec. 31, 2018>
  (2) Except as otherwise provided for in this Act, the provisions on limited-liability companies under the Commercial Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to matters concerning tax accounting corporations.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

CHAPTER V DISCIPLINARY ACTION

Article 17 (Disciplinary Action) (1) If a certified tax accountant falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance may issue an order for disciplinary action prescribed in paragraph (2) following a resolution by the Certified Tax Accountant Disciplinary Committee: <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  1. Where he or she violates this Act;
  2. Where he or she violates regulations of the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants.
  (2) Types of disciplinary action against a certified tax accountant shall be as follows:
  1. Revocation of registration;
  2. Suspension of business for a period not exceeding two years;
  3. An administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won;
  4. Censure.
  (3) Where the registration of a certified tax accountant requested to be disciplined by the Certified Tax Accountant Disciplinary Committee has been revoked in accordance with subparagraph 3 or 4 of Article 7, the Minister of Economy and Finance may reject registration referred to in Article 6 within a prescribed period not exceeding five years following a resolution by the Certified Tax Accountant Disciplinary Committee.
  (4) No disciplinary action prescribed in paragraphs (1) through (3) shall be taken when three years have passed from the date on which a reason for the relevant disciplinary action arises.
  (5) If a certified tax accountant fails to pay an administrative fine imposed under paragraph (2) 3 by the payment deadline, the Minister of Economy and Finance may collect it in the same manner as delinquent national taxes are collected.
  (6) Where issuing an order for disciplinary action under paragraph (1), the Minister of Economy and Finance shall record and manage the results of disciplinary action including grounds for and details of the disciplinary action, whether or not he or she is a certified tax accountant who resigned as public official, and others prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly Inserted on Dec. 31, 2018>
  (7) Where the Minister of Economy and Finance issues an order to take disciplinary action against a certified tax accountant pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall notify the relevant certified tax accountant, Association he or she is affiliated with, and the Commissioner of the National Tax Service without delay, specifying the grounds for such disciplinary action, and publish an announcement of the details thereof in the Official Gazette or on the website of the Ministry of Economy and Finance. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (8) Upon receipt of notification under paragraph (7), the Association he or she is affiliated with shall publish the details thereof by posting them on its website for at least three months. <Newly Inserted on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (9) Matters necessary for the organization, operation, etc. of the Certified Tax Accountant Disciplinary Committee, the notification and public announcement under paragraph (7), and publication under paragraph (8) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2018; Nov. 23, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

CHAPTER VI KOREAN ASSOCIATION OF CERTIFIED PUBLIC TAX ACCOUNTANTS

Article 18 (Establishment and Supervision) (1) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall be established in order to promote the dignity of certified tax accountants, promote the improvement and development of their practices, and execute administrative affairs relating to guidance for and supervision over certified tax accountants.
  (2) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall be a corporation, and certified tax accountants shall be its members.
  (3) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall establish regulations and obtain authorization therefor from the Minister of Economy and Finance before incorporation.
  (4) Where the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants intends to amend its regulations, it shall obtain approval therefor from the Minister of Economy and Finance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) Matters necessary for the establishment, operation, etc. of the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants and matters that shall be included in regulations of the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2013]

Article 18-2 (Training for Members) (1) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall conduct training courses for the following persons and shall guide and supervise self-training activities of members: <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013; Mar. 2, 2016; Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. Members;
  2. Clerks, etc. employed under Article 12-5.
  (2) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall have a Taxation Training Institute to conduct the training referred to in paragraph (1). <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  (3) Necessary matters concerning the training and supervision referred to in paragraph (1) shall be determined by the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants with approval from the Minister of Economy and Finance. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 18-3 (Entrustment of Affairs) (1) A public institution may entrust the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants with affairs or seek advice about matters within the scope of the services of certified tax accountants pursuant to Article 2. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  (2) Where the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants is entrusted with affairs or requested to give advice pursuant to paragraph (1), it may authorize any of its members to carry out such affairs or provide advice. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 18-4 (Obligation of Cooperation for Public Representation) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants shall fully cooperate in the efficient operation of the public representation system by supporting tax agent services of public representatives under Article 59-2 of the Framework Act on National Taxes. <Amended on Dec. 31, 2018>
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 31, 2018]

Article 19 (Expulsion of Members) The Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants may expel a member who degrades certified tax accountants' dignity or who violates the regulations of the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants, with approval from the Minister of Economy and Finance. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

CHAPTER VI-2 FOREIGN CERTIFIED TAX CONSULTANT AND FOREIGN CERTIFIED TAX ACCOUNTING CORPORATION

Article 19-2 (Definitions) The terms used in this Chapter are defined as follows:
  1. The term "foreign-certified tax consultant" means a person qualified as a tax specialist in his or her home country and whose qualification as a foreign-certified tax consultant is approved by the Minister of Economy and Finance pursuant to Article 19-3:
  2. The term "private office for foreign tax consulting services" means an office established by a foreign-certified tax consultant to provide tax services referred to in Article 19-7 in Korea;
  3. The term "foreign-certified tax accounting corporation" means a tax accounting corporation incorporated in accordance with statutes and regulations of a country, other than the Republic of Korea, and the head office of which is located in such country, or any organization equivalent thereto;
  4. The term "corporate office for foreign tax consulting services" means an office established by a foreign-certified tax accounting corporation to provide tax services referred to in Article 19-7 in Korea;
  5. The term "treaty, etc." means a free trade agreement or any other agreements, concluded between the Republic of Korea and a foreign country (including a union of States, such as a confederation and an economic community) to provide foreign tax services referred to in Article 19-7 in each party to an agreement, and entered into force in each party to an agreement;
  6. The term "home country of qualification" means a country prescribed by Presidential Decree, in which a foreign-certified tax consultant is qualified as a tax specialist and which is a party to the relevant treaty, etc.: Provided, That where a country has several states, provinces, autonomous districts, etc. granting qualification to be recognized only within the relevant area in accordance with Acts of the country, each of such states, provinces, autonomous districts, etc. shall be deemed a home country of qualification.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-3 (Qualification Approval of Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants) (1) Any person qualified as a tax specialist in the home country of qualification and intending to become a foreign-certified tax consultant in Korea shall obtain qualification approval of a foreign-certified tax consultant from the Minister of Economy and Finance.
  (2) Any person intending to apply for qualification approval of a foreign-certified tax consultant pursuant to paragraph (1) (hereinafter referred to as "applicant for qualification approval") shall submit an application to the Minister of Economy and Finance, along with the following documents: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A document attesting that he or she has been qualified as a tax specialist in the home country of qualification;
  2. A document attesting that he or she has at least three years of work experience as a tax specialist in the home country of qualification;
  3. A document certifying that he or she does not fall under any ground for disqualification as a certified tax consultant referred to in Article 4 and a document promising that he or she is willing to or able to perform his or her duties conscientiously and appropriately;
  4. A document attesting that he or she has a place in Korea where any document, etc. can be served.
  (3) A document to be attached under paragraph (2) shall be an original or certified copy thereof, and a document not in Korean shall be accompanied by a notarized translation in Korean.
  (4) The detailed scope of tax specialists recognized in the home country of qualification shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) Matters concerning the preparation and submission of applications for qualification approval shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-4 (Issuance of Certificates of Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants) (1) The Minister of Economy and Finance shall verify the details of documents submitted by applicants for qualification approval pursuant to Article 19-3 and issue a certificate as a foreign-certified tax consultant to an applicant who has submitted a complete application for qualification approval.
  (2) When the Minister of Economy and Finance rejects an application for qualification approval, he or she shall, without delay, notify the applicant of the purport of and ground for such rejection.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-5 (Registration of Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants) (1) A foreign-certified tax consultant intending to provide services referred to in Article 19-7 shall register his or her name in the register of foreign-certified tax consultants kept by the Ministry of Economy and Finance.
  (2) If a change occurs to any registered matter with regard to a foreign-certified tax consultant registered pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall report to the Minister of Economy and Finance thereon, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly Inserted on Jan. 1, 2013>
  (3) Matters necessary for the procedure for registration under paragraph (1), accompanying documents, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-6 (Revocation of Registration of Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants) (1) Where a foreign-certified tax consultant falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance shall revoke his or her registration:
  1. Where he or she is disqualified as a tax specialist or his or her qualification as a tax specialist is suspended in the home country of qualification;
  2. Where he or she becomes disqualified under Article 4 (including cases where he or she becomes disqualified under Article 4 in accordance with statutes and regulations of the home country of qualification);
  3. Where he or she makes false entry in an application for registration or falsely states important matters in an attached document;
  4. Where he or she reports the discontinuation of his or her business;
  5. Where he or she is deceased.
  (2) When the Minister of Economy and Finance revokes registration pursuant to paragraph (1), he or she shall notify the relevant foreign-certified tax consultant of such revocation, with the grounds therefor clearly specified.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-7 (Scope of Services) A foreign-certified tax consultant shall provide the following services with the authority delegated by a taxpayer, etc.:
  1. Consultations or advices on tax-related statutes and regulations and taxation systems of the home country of his or her qualification;
  2. Consultations or advices on international taxes prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-8 (Methods of Providing Services by Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants) A foreign-certified tax consultant who has completed registration pursuant to Article 19-5 shall provide services referred to in Article 19-7 only by any of the following methods:
  1. Providing services after establishing one private office for foreign tax consulting services;
  2. Providing services after being employed as a foreign-certified tax consultant by a private office for foreign tax consulting services;
  3. Providing services after being affiliated with or employed by a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services;
  4. Providing services after being employed as a foreign-certified tax consultant by a tax accounting corporation established under Article 16-3.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-9 (Registration of Corporate Offices for Foreign Tax Consulting Services) (1) Where a foreign-certified tax accounting corporation establishes a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services and provides services referred to in Article 19-7 through such corporate office, it shall file for registration with the Minister of Economy and Finance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) If a change occurs to any registered matter with regard to a foreign-certified tax accounting corporation registered pursuant to paragraph (1), the corporation shall report to the Minister of Economy and Finance thereon, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Newly Inserted on Jan. 1, 2013>
  (3) Matters necessary for the requirements for registration under paragraph (1), accompanying documents, procedures for registration, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 1, 2013>
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-10 (Revocation of Registration of Corporate Offices for Foreign Tax Consulting Services) Where a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services registered under Article 19-9 falls under any of the following cases, the Minister of Economy and Finance may revoke its registration or issue an order to wholly or partially suspend its business operations for up to one year: Provided, That in cases falling under subparagraph 1 or 2, registration thereof shall be revoked: <Amended on Dec. 29, 2015; Mar. 2, 2016>
  1. Where a foreign-certified tax accounting corporation is subject to a disposition to revoke registration or suspend business in the home country of qualification;
  2. Where it falsely states the important matters in an application for registration or a document attached thereto;
  3. Where it violates Articles 12, 12-2 through 12-5, 15, 16-7 and 16-11 applied mutatis mutandis in accordance with Articles 19-7, 19-11 (3), 19-12, 19-13, and 19-15.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-11 (Representation of Qualification) (1) Where a foreign-certified tax consultant identifies himself or herself in providing services, he or she shall use, in his or her title, the phrase "tax consultant", following the name of the home country of qualification: Provided, that where his or her home country of qualification is a certain area of one country, such as a state, province, autonomous district, he or she may use, the phrase "tax consultant", following the name of the home country of qualification in which the certain area is located.
  (2) A private office for foreign tax consulting services shall use, in its title, the phrase "office for tax consulting services" after indicating the name of the home country of qualification and the name of a foreign-certified tax consultant, while a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services shall use, in its title, the phrase "office for tax consulting services" after indicating the name of the home country of qualification and the name of the head office.
  (3) An office for tax consulting services under paragraph (2) shall post a notice of the home country of qualification of a foreign-certified private tax consultant or foreign-certified corporation-affiliated tax consultant at an appropriate place of such office in a public-friendly manner.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-12 (Responsibilities of Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants) (1) No current or former foreign-certified tax consultant or his or her current or former clerk shall divulge any confidential information he or she has learned in the course of performing his or her duties, except as otherwise provided in other statutes or regulations. <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  (2) A foreign-certified tax consultant shall stay in Korea for at least 180 days a year, except in any of the following cases: Provided, That the period for which a foreign-certified tax consultant stays overseas due to his or her own or his or her relative's injury or illness or any other unavoidable cause shall be deemed the period of his or her stay in Korea: <Amended on Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. Where he or she is employed by a private office for foreign tax consulting services;
  2. Where he or she is employed by a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services;
  3. Where he or she is employed by a tax accounting corporation established under Article 16-3.
  (3) Where a foreign-certified tax consultant or a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services ceases to be qualified as a tax specialist in the home country of qualification or a foreign-certified tax accounting corporation is subject to a disposition to revoke registration or suspend business in the home country of qualification, he or she or it shall, without delay, report thereon to the Minister of Economy and Finance.
  (4) When a foreign-certified tax consultant or a corporate office for foreign tax consulting services commences, suspends or discontinues business operations or establishes, relocates or closes its office, he or she shall, without delay, report thereon to the Minister of Economy and Finance.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-13 (Prohibition of Employment and Partnership) (1) No foreign-certified tax consultant or corporate office for foreign tax consulting services shall employ a certified tax accountant registered under Article 6 (1).
  (2) No foreign-certified tax consultant or corporate office for foreign tax consulting services shall enter into a joint contract for, or jointly provide, services referred to in Article 19-7 with a certified tax accountant or tax accounting corporation, and accordingly share compensation or proceeds therefrom.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Jun. 30, 2011]

Article 19-14 (Investment of Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants to Tax Accounting Corporations) The Foreign-Certified Tax Consultants may make investments to a tax accounting corporation established pursuant to Article 16-3 to the extent of less than 50/100 of the investment equities with the voting rights or the total capital amount of such tax accounting corporation. In such cases, the investment amount of each foreign-certified tax consultant shall be less than 10/100 of the investment equities with the voting rights or the total capital amount of such tax accounting corporation.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 2, 2016]
  [Previous Article 19-14 moved to Article 19-15 <Mar. 2, 2016>]

Article 19-15 (Provisions Applicable Mutatis Mutandis) @Articles 6 (2), (3) 1 and (4), 12, 12-2 through 12-5, 13 (1), 14, 14-2, 15, 16-2, 16-4 (2) 2 and 3, 16-4 (3), 16-7, 16-10, 16-11, 16-13, 16-15 (2) through (5), 17, 18 (2), 19, 20, and 24 shall apply mutatis mutandis to foreign-certified tax consultants and corporate offices for foreign tax consulting services. <Amended on Dec. 29, 2015; Mar. 2, 2016; Dec. 31, 2018; Nov. 23, 2021>
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 1, 2013]
  [Moved from Article 19-14 <Mar. 2, 2016>]

CHAPTER VII SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 20 (Restriction on Services) (1) No person, other than those who have registered under Article 6, shall provide tax agent services: Provided, That this shall not apply where he or she provides tax agent services as duties of an attorney-at-law pursuant to Article 3 of the Attorney-at-Law Act and where he or she has registered under Article 20-2 (1). <Amended on Nov. 23, 2021>
  (2) No person, other than those who have registered under Article 6, shall use the title of a certified tax accountant or other titles similar thereto.
  (3) None of the persons who shall not provide tax agent services pursuant to paragraph (1) shall represent or advertise anything to the effect that he or she provides tax agent services: Provided, That this shall not apply where such services are included in the scope of services of any person prescribed by other Acts.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]
  [Paragraph (1) of this Article was amended following the decision of nonconformity to the Constitution by the Constitutional Court on April 26, 2018 in accordance with Act No. 18521 (Nov. 23, 2021)]

Article 20-2 (Registration of Tax Agent Services) (1) Where any of the following persons intends to provide tax agent services, he or she shall be registered in the register of tax agent services classified as follows, which is kept in the Ministry of Economy and Finance:
  1. Certified public accountants registered under the Certified Public Accountant Act (excluding certified public accountants eligible to be registered in the register of certified tax accountants under Article 2 (1) of the Addenda to the Certified Tax Accountant Act (Act No. 7032): The register of tax agent services for certified public accountants;
  2. An attorney-at-law registered under the Attorney-at-Law Act (excluding an attorney-at-law who is eligible to be registered in the register of certified tax accountants under Article 2 (1) of the Addenda to the Certified Tax Accountant Act (Act No. 7032)), who is deemed qualified as a certified tax accountant under Article 2 of the Addenda to the Certified Public Accountant Act (No. 15288): The register of tax agent services for attorney-at-laws.
  (2) The duties of an attorney-at-law referred to in paragraph (1) 2 shall be limited to the acts or duties provided in subparagraphs 1, 2, and 4 through 7 of Article 2, among tax agent services, and other duties incidental thereto.
  (3) An attorney-at-law referred to in paragraph (1) 2 shall receive in-service education for at least one month in order to be registered in the register of tax agent services.
  (4) The subjects of in-service education, place, timing, methods, and procedures of in-service education under paragraph (3) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (5) Articles 1-2, 2-2, 4, 9 through 12, 12-2 through 12-5, 13, 14 (excluding an attorney-at-law from application mutatis mutandis), 14-2, 14-3, 15, 16, 16-2, and 17 (excluding paragraph (1) 2 of that Article) and Chapter VIII shall apply mutatis mutandis. In such cases, "certified tax accountant" shall be construed as "certified public accountant or attorney-at-law"; "Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants" as "Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants"; and "Article 6" as "Article 20-2 (1), respectively.
  (6) Articles 6 through 8 shall apply mutatis mutandis to registration under paragraph (1). In such cases, "where he or she fails to receive in-service education referred to in Article 12-6 (1)" in Article 6 (3) 2 shall be construed as "where he or she fails to receive in-service education referred to in Article 20-2 (3)."
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Nov. 23, 2021]
  [Enforcement Date: Nov. 24, 2022] Article 20-2 (5) (limited to the provisions regarding Article 14-3)

Article 20-3 (Delegation of Authority and Entrustment of Duties) (1) The Minister of Economy and Finance may delegate part of his or her authority vested under this Act to the Commissioner of the National Tax Service, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (2) The Minister of Economy and Finance may entrust his or her duties concerning a qualification examination for certified public accountants pursuant to Article 5 to a corporation incorporated for the purpose of the qualification examination, etc., as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
  (3) The Minister of Economy and Finance may entrust the Korean Association of Certified Public Tax Accountants with affairs related to the registration of the following persons as certified tax accountants, among registration-related affairs assigned to him or her under Articles 6 through 8, as prescribed by Presidential Decree: <Newly Inserted on May 2, 2011; Jan. 1, 2013; Jun. 9, 2020>
  1. A person qualified as a certified tax accountant, after passing a qualification examination for certified tax accountants under Article 5;
  2. A person qualified as a certified tax accountant under paragraph (2) of the Addenda to the Certified Tax Accountant Act (Act No. 2358);
  3. A person qualified as a certified tax accountant under paragraph (3) (referring to the amended provisions in accordance with the Certified Tax Accountant Act (Act No. 6837)) of the Addenda to the Certified Tax Accountant Act (Act No. 6080).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]
  [Title Amended on May 2, 2011]

Article 21 (Re-Examination of Regulation) The Minister of Economy and Finance shall examine the appropriateness of the following matters every three years (the period ending on the day immediately before every third anniversary of the base date) and shall take measures, such as making improvements:
  1. Matters to be specified in the articles of incorporation of tax accounting corporations referred to in Article 16-3 (2): January 1, 2016;
  2. Matters concerning the registration, and requirements and refusal thereof, of tax accounting corporations referred to in Article 16-4: January 1, 2016;
  3. Matters concerning grounds for dissolution of tax accounting corporations, the notification of the fact of the occurrence of grounds for dissolution, and the deposit of the compensation reserve referred to in Article 16-13: January 1, 2016;
  4. Amended matters of the articles of incorporation, which are to be reported by tax accounting corporations referred to in Article 16-14: January 1, 2016.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Dec. 29, 2015]

Article 21-2 (Legal Fiction as Public Official in Application of Penalty Provisions) Among the members of the Certified Tax Accountant Disciplinary Committee, those who are not public officials shall be deemed to be public officials in applying Articles 129 through 132 of the Criminal Act.
  [This Article Newly Inserted on Mar. 2, 2016]

CHAPTER VIII PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 22 (Penalty Provisions) (1) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2011>
  1. Any person providing tax agent services without qualification as a certified tax accountant;
  2. Any person divulging any confidential information he or she has learned in the course of performing his or her duties, in violation of Articles 11 (including cases where that Article is applied mutatis mutandis under Article 16-16 (1)) and 19-12 (1).
  (2) Any certified tax accountant abetting a person in a crime prescribed in the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and a crime relating to the duties of public officials prescribed in the Criminal Act shall be punished by aggravating by 1/3 of a term of imprisonment or a fine referred to in the relevant provisions applicable thereto.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 22-2 (Penalty Provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2011; Mar. 2, 2016; Nov. 23, 2021>
  1. A person who introduces or arranges for the introduction of tax agent services and receives or demands the consideration therefor, in violation of Article 2-2 (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Article 20-2 (5));
  2. A person eligible to provide tax agent services pursuant to this Act, but who provides tax agent services without registration, in violation of Article 6 or 20-2 (1);
  3. A person who lends his or her title, etc., in violation of Article 12-3 (1) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Articles 16-16 (1) and 19-15);
  4. A person who borrows a title, etc., in violation of Article 12-3 (2) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Articles 16-16 (1) and 19-15);
  5. A person who arranges for the lending of a title, etc., in violation of Article 12-3 (3) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Articles 16-16 (1) and 19-15);
  6. A person who is awarded a contract, in violation of Article 14-3 (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Article 20-2 (5));
  7. A person who uses the name a tax accounting corporation or certified tax accountant or any other name similar thereto without registration, in violation of Article 16-9 (2) or 20 (2) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Article 19-15);
  8. A person subject to an order to suspend his or her business or whose registration has been rejected pursuant to Article 17 (including where that Article is applied mutatis mutandis under Article 19-15), but who provides tax agent services during the period of the suspension of business or the rejection of registration;
  9. A person qualified as a tax specialist in the home country of qualification, but who fails to obtain qualification approval under Article 19-3 or provides services referred to in Article 19-7 without registration pursuant to Article 19-5.
  10. A person who represents or advertises anything prohibited by Article 20 (3) (including cases applied mutatis mutandis in Article 19-15);
  11. A person who performs the acts or duties under subparagraph 3 or 8 of Article 2, in violation of Article 20-2 (2).
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jan. 30, 2009]

Article 23 (Penalty Provisions) Any of the following persons shall be punished by a fine not exceeding two million won: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2011; Mar. 2, 2016>
  1. Any person violating Article 13 (including where that Article is applied mutatis mutandis under Article 19-15), such as violating matters concerning the establishment of offices;
